references.text: The parallel account in Exodus where Moses throws the tablets and breaks them at the foot of the mountain because of the people's sin with the golden calf.
Describes the two stone tablets that God gave to Moses, written with God's finger, which are the same tablets that were broken.
God commands Moses to carve out two new stone tablets to replace those that were broken.
The continuation of the account where God tells Moses to carve out new tablets to replace the broken ones.
Refers to the two stone tablets that Moses placed in the ark at Horeb, and confirms that new tablets replaced the broken ones.
Paul refers to the stone tablets and contrasts the stone tablets of the old covenant with the heart's tablets of the new covenant.
